why: The two sides put different M-polyfold structures on different carriers. In A, Obj F G is a nested subtype of ObjX × objRight G, with objRight G ⊆ MorY × ObjZ. Its structure PObj F G h is the iterated sub-M-polyfold structure: objRight ⊆ 𝐘 × Z first, then objSet ⊆ X × PA G (likewise for morphisms). A's hypothesis is Admissible F G (F or G a local sc-diffeomorphism), weaker than B's F.IsEquivalence. In B, the objects are a subtype of the flat triple product with the sub-M-polyfold structure of X × (𝐘 × Z), and the text says the same. A ⇒ B needs two things. (i) objSetB and morSetB are sub-M-polyfolds of the triple products: a transitivity/product lemma for sub-M-polyfolds, or the text's retraction (10.8). (ii) The ep-groupoid must be transported along the entrywise homeomorphisms objHomeo/morHomeo, as sc-diffeomorphisms PObj ≅ subPolyfold hS, including condition (4) on 𝐋 ₛ×ₜ 𝐋. Neither is in the project; its header says the comparison with the triple-product structure 'is not needed below'. This is standard Part I mathematics, believed true, but well beyond glue. B ⇒ A fails for the same reason in reverse: A's lemmas concern the project's own carriers and structures, and A also contains five general helpers. Partial results proved: A_to_BIter assembles A's lemmas (not the definition epGroupoid) into an ep-groupoid on the project's carriers with groupoid F G, PObj and PMor for an equivalence F. objHomeo/morHomeo show the carriers are entrywise homeomorphic to B's subtypes. With V10_17, this puts the whole gap in the two M-polyfold structures, iterated versus triple-product.
